articles.title: US formalises removal of three Pakistan-linked men from sanctions list - Social News XYZ
articles.summary: US formalises removal of three Pakistan-linked men from sanctions list  Social News XYZ
articles.full_text:
Washington, Oct 7 (SocialNews.XYZ) The United States has formally published the removal from its sanctions list of three Pakistan-linked men who had been designated more than two decades ago in cases involving terrorism and narcotics trafficking, according to the Treasury Department records.
The three are Mohammed Tufail, Sher Afghan and Nasir Ali Khan.
The removals were originally made by the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control on July 27 as part of a broader effort to modernise its sanctions lists. They were formally published in the Federal Register on Wednesday.
Treasury said the July action removed 84 individuals and entities and updated other entries as part of an effort to keep US sanctions targeted, effective and current.
Those removed included individuals and entities no longer considered US national-security or foreign-policy priorities, including some deceased people, defunct entities and targets sanctioned more than 20 years ago. Treasury did not publicly specify which rationale applied to each of the three Pakistan-linked individuals.
Tufail, also identified as S M Tufail and Sheik Mohammed Tufail, had been designated under US terrorism sanctions.
When his assets were blocked in December 2001, the Treasury Department identified him as an industrialist and one of three key directors of Ummah Tameer-e-Nau, or UTN, an organisation founded by Pakistani nuclear scientists.
Treasury said at the time that UTN directors and members had met Osama bin Laden, al-Qaeda leaders and Taliban leader Mullah Omar and discussed the development of chemical, biological and nuclear weapons.
The other two men were designated under US narcotics sanctions.
Sher Afghan, also identified by aliases including Shir Afghan, Mohammad Aziz and Abdullah Khan, was born in Pakistan and was added to the sanctions list in June 2001 under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act.
Nasir Ali Khan, born in Pakistan in 1955, was also placed under narcotics sanctions in June 2001.
A State Department report covering Pakistan's counter-narcotics efforts in 1996 said the country's caretaker government had arrested a major trafficker named Nasir Ali Khan who was wanted in the United States on drug charges. The report also said an American extradition request was pending.
The available records do not establish in the sanctions-removal notice why each of the three men was taken off the list in July.
OFAC said its broader sanctions-modernisation exercise was intended to remove outdated entries and improve the accuracy of its lists while ensuring removals did not undermine US national-security or foreign-policy interests.
Source: IANS

articles.title: OFAC Targets Iran’s Aviation and Rail Sectors for Additional Sanctions - Thompson Hine
articles.summary: OFAC Targets Iran’s Aviation and Rail Sectors for Additional Sanctions  Thompson Hine
articles.full_text:
On October 1, 2026, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued new sectoral sanctions determinations targeting Iran’s automotive and rail sectors. These determinations authorize OFAC to sanction any entity or individual operating in these sectors. OFAC stated that Iran’s automotive sector is the country’s largest economic sector outside of oil and gas and remains a core contributor to Iran’s industrial base and is a major revenue generator for the regime. OFAC has also targeted Iran’s rail sector stating that, given the maritime blockade, the Iranian regime is using its railway companies to transport oil and sustain regional trade. In addition to these new automotive and rails sectoral sanctions, OFAC also announced additional designations and placement on the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List of multiple Iranian and third-country entities and individuals involved in the Iranian heavy equipment, mining, metals, steel and oil networks. Additional information on OFAC targeting of Iran’s automotive, rail, manufacturing, and steel industrial sectors is available here.
Specific identifying information on newly sanctioned entities and persons under these aviation and rail sectoral sanctions is available here. As a result of these actions, all property and interests in property of these designated or blocked persons that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.
Further, OFAC has issued a revised FAQ to assist in guidance on how it defines the sectors of the Iranain economy under its sectoral sanctions.
With these most recent sanctions, Iran’s oil, aviation, automotive and rail sectors are now targeted as being industrial sectors providing revenue to the Iranian regime and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). For additional information on OFAC sanctions, see SmarTrade updates of September 11, 2026, August 25, 2026, and February 12, 2026.

articles.title: Biren’s Conditional HK$4bn Share Deal Tests AI Chip Growth - streamlinefeed.co.ke
articles.summary: Biren’s Conditional HK$4bn Share Deal Tests AI Chip Growth  streamlinefeed.co.ke
articles.full_text:
Biren Technology conditionally agreed to place 130 million new shares for HK$4.04bn gross, but the deal is not complete and remains subject to listing and legal conditions.
A conditional follow-on, not a new listing
Biren signed the placing agreement on October 8, offering new H shares at HK$31.08 apiece through CICC Hong Kong Securities and UBS’s Hong Kong branch. The company estimates gross proceeds of HK$4.04bn and net proceeds of HK$4.02bn after expenses. At the exchange rate used in financial coverage, the net amount is about US$515m.
The price is 9.76% below the previous day’s close and 13.73% below the five-day average, according to the filing. If all shares are placed, they would equal 5% of existing share capital and 4.76% of the enlarged total. The company was already listed on Hong Kong’s main board in January; this is an additional capital raising, not an initial public offering.
The deal remains conditional on matters including approval to list the new shares and delivery of required documentation. Biren says the agreement can terminate if conditions are not met or waived by October 15, and the placing agents have termination rights. The proposed investors are not named; the filing says the placement is expected to involve at least six independent investors.
- 130 million new H shares at HK$31.08 each.
- Estimated proceeds: HK$4.04bn gross and HK$4.02bn net.
- Potential dilution: 4.76% of enlarged share capital.
- Status: conditionally agreed, not yet completed.
Production spending is the stated reason
Biren says it plans to direct 70% of the net proceeds to supply-chain procurement, production readiness and commercialisation of next-generation products. Another 20% is earmarked for research and development and its software ecosystem, with 10% for working capital and general corporate needs. Those categories describe the company’s stated plan, not a guarantee of commercial success.
The filing says the next-generation product has completed initial bring-up and entered post-silicon validation, with sampling and volume production expected over coming quarters subject to validation and customer qualification. The company cites rising customer demand, longer supply lead times and higher procurement costs as reasons it needs to move faster. Those are management’s explanations; the announcement does not independently verify demand or product readiness.
Biren completed a HK$7.07bn placement in July. Its October filing says that by September 30, only HK$814.8m—about 19%—of proceeds allocated to production and commercialisation had been used; it expects the balance to be substantially used by year-end. The earlier raise was not exhausted; the company says its spending timetable has accelerated.
Rapid revenue growth sits beside large losses
Biren’s audited 2025 report shows a growing but loss-making business. Revenue rose to RMB1.03bn from RMB336.8m in 2024, while operating loss was RMB1.04bn. The RMB16.49bn net loss included RMB15.47bn in finance costs from revaluing redemption liabilities that ended upon listing. Its company-defined adjusted loss was RMB873.8m.
For the first half of 2026, the company reported unaudited revenue of RMB1.24bn, compared with RMB58.9m in the same period last year. Its loss narrowed to RMB377.2m, while the adjusted loss was RMB337.2m. At the same time, three customers accounted for roughly 74.5% of first-half revenue, underscoring concentration risk as the company scales sales.
The numbers make the fundraising story more complicated than a simple growth narrative. Revenue is rising quickly and adjusted losses have narrowed, but the business is spending heavily on research and production. The new issue would dilute existing shareholders, and its discounted price is below both the previous day’s market close and the July placing price.
Export controls shape the supply-chain backdrop
Biren’s filings and US export-control records place the company within a wider contest over advanced computing. The US Commerce Department added Biren-related entities to the Entity List in 2023 and later updated an alias. Under US rules, some exports, re-exports or transfers of items subject to the Export Administration Regulations may require a licence, with strict review policies applying to listed parties.
This is not a blanket ban on every Biren product or on investors buying shares in Hong Kong. Restrictions depend on the item, transaction and supply chain, and the October placing announcement does not say export controls caused the capital raise. They are a relevant operating constraint for a chip designer that relies on manufacturing ecosystems and equipment spanning multiple countries.
What investors and customers should watch
The immediate milestone is whether the placement closes by the stated deadline and on what terms. Then comes product validation, customer qualification and repeat revenue. The filings show growth opportunities alongside capital needs and concentration risk.
- Closing is conditional; the net proceeds are not yet secured.
- The new shares would dilute existing holders.
- Production plans depend on validation and customer qualification.
- Three customers generated nearly three-quarters of H1 revenue.
No direct Kenyan customer, subsidiary or investment relationship is identified in the company’s filings. The wider significance is indirect: more domestic Chinese accelerator capacity could affect global competition and the range of compute suppliers available to cloud operators. Any impact on Kenyan prices, procurement or access remains an inference, not an announced outcome of this transaction.
